record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity
record.context_brief: Maximal randomized versus quantum query separation
record.original_question: For a total Boolean function f:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, with D(f), R(f), and Q(f) denoting deterministic, bounded-error randomized, and bounded-error quantum query complexity, respectively, what is the largest possible gap between R(f) and Q(f)?

evidence.quote: Given a total Boolean function f :{0, 1}n→{ 0, 1}, we denote by D ( f), R (f), and Q ( f) the deterministic, (bounded-error) randomized, and (bounded-error) quantum query complexities of f respectively.
Yet all this progress, as dramatic as it’s been, still leaves a gap between 3 and 4 in the exponent of the optimal separation between R ( f) and Q (f).
Problem 4 What is the largest possible gap between R (f) and Q (f), for a total Boolean function f?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f : {0,1}^n -> {0,1} be a total Boolean function. Define the following query complexity measures, where an algorithm has access to the input x ∈ {0,1}^n only via queries of the form "what is x_i?":

- D(f): the deterministic query complexity, the minimum over deterministic decision trees computing f(x) on every input x of the worst-case number of queries.
- R(f): the bounded-error randomized query complexity, the minimum number of queries needed by a randomized algorithm that outputs f(x) with probability at least 2/3 on every input x.
- Q(f): the bounded-error quantum query complexity, the minimum number of quantum (oracle) queries needed by a quantum algorithm that outputs f(x) with probability at least 2/3 on every input x.

Determine the largest possible asymptotic gap between R(f) and Q(f) over all total Boolean functions f. More precisely, determine the supremum of all real α ≥ 1 such that there exists an infinite family of total Boolean functions {f_n} with

   R(f_n) = Ω̃( Q(f_n)^α ),

and prove a matching upper bound R(f) = O( Q(f)^α · polylog ) valid for every total Boolean function f. It is known that 3 ≤ α ≤ 4; identify the exact value.
artifact.status_search_result: For total Boolean functions, the best known lower-bound separation gives R(f) = Ω̃(Q(f)^3) (Aaronson–Ben-David–Kothari–Rao–Tal, 2020/2021), while the best general upper bound remains R(f) = O(Q(f)^4) (Aaronson–Ben-David–Kothari). Sherstov–Storozhenko–Wu (STOC 2021; SICOMP 2023) settled the analogous question optimally for partial functions, but the total-function case remains open: the exponent is known only to lie in [3,4]. No resolution closing this gap has appeared as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: An Optimal Separation of Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal separation for partial Boolean functions; total-function case not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: The optimal separation result of Sherstov–Storozhenko–Wu applies to partial, not total, Boolean functions.

status_evidence.title: Separations in Query Complexity Based on Pointer Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs total Boolean functions with super-quadratic R vs Q separations.
status_evidence.claim: Cubic-type separations for total functions established; exponent 4 upper bound not matched.

status_evidence.title: A Super-Grover Separation Between Randomized and Quantum Query Complexities
status_evidence.snippet: Total Boolean function with R(f)=Ω̃(Q(f)^{5/2}), refuting R=O(Q^2) conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Exponent in optimal R vs Q separation for total functions exceeds 2.
